title: Answer: experimenter free will survives in the compatibilist sense

statements.text: A locally causal theory constrained by the invariant set postulate accommodates the compatibilist notion of experimenter free will. Free will should be defined without counterfactuals, as the absence of constraints that prevent doing what one wants.

sources.quote: the theory readily accommodates the classical compatibilist notion of (experimenter) free will
by saying that I am free if there are no constraints preventing me from doing what I want to do
